entries.name: (2014) Ray tracing with OpenGL Compute Shaders

entries.name: A Trip Down the Graphics Pipeline
entries.description: by Jim Blinn - Popular book that contains wealth information about the graphics pipeline, and of the best sources to learn the core concepts of Computer Graphics.

entries.name: Computer Graphics
entries.description: by John F. Hughes, et al. - Computer Graphics is indeed a must for anyone being involved in the design and implementation of Computer Graphics algorithms. However, this is not a OpenGL focused book, but contains valuable demonstrations of the technology.

entries.name: Interactive Computer Graphics
entries.description: by Edward Angel and Dave Shreiner - It provides several examples using OpenGL and it covers several aspects at once, but if you are trying to learn OpenGL on your own you might not find this helpful.

entries.name: OpenGL ES 3.0 Programming Guide
entries.description: by Dan Ginsburg, et al. - It presents all the necessary information to use the OpenGL ES 3.0 API in a clear manner.

entries.name: OpenGL Insights
entries.description: by Patrick Cozzi, Christophe Riccio - Rich and comprehensive resource to learn techniques and tips, covering several advanced topics of OpenGL.

entries.name: OpenGL Programming Guide
entries.description: by Dave Shreiner, et al. - It does a good job covering the basics and providing clear reference of the API.

entries.name: OpenGL Shading Language
entries.description: by Randi J. Rost, et al. - Very clear and well written book about Shading Language. Also, it provides several explanations of writing shaders.

entries.name: OpenGL SuperBible
entries.description: by Richard S. Wright, et al. - It covers the basic concepts of computer graphics and provides clear examples using OpenGL. Definitely, it is a must for beginners.

entries.name: Real-Time Rendering
entries.description: by Tomas Akenine-Moller, Eric Haines and Naty Hoffman - It does a good job at explaining concepts for game engine, basis for game client programming as well as the necessary knowledge for understanding DirectX and OpenGL.
